text:
The strongest ground is that the promise was oral: many jurisdictions require a signed writing to revive a debt the statute of limitations has barred, and the oral promise lacks one. Lack of consideration is weaker, because Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82 treats a promise to pay a time-barred debt as binding without new consideration. The overheard "deadbeat" remark neither supplies consideration nor amounts to duress.

CONFIDENCE: 60
